stories.title: JEE Main applicants can now just fill the form again
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency says JEE Main 2027 Session 1 applicants who entered wrong details such as name, category or qualifications can submit a fresh form until November 22. Taking the exam on more than one application number will be treated as unfair practice.

stories.title: Over 10 lakh register for UGC NET December 2026
stories.summary: More than 10 lakh candidates registered for UGC NET December 2026 before registration closed on October 31, according to NTA figures. Around 1.62 lakh had still not paid the exam fee, and registration alone does not confirm candidature.

stories.title: NEET SS 2026 registration opens until November 18
stories.summary: NBEMS has opened registration for NEET Super Specialty 2026 at natboard.edu.in, with applications due by November 18. Candidates need an MD, MS, DNB or equivalent completed by that date and must be registered with a medical council.

stories.title: AIIMS declares INI SS stage 1 results for January 2027
stories.summary: AIIMS New Delhi has published INI-SS stage 1 results for the January 2027 session at aiimsexams.ac.in. The list shows 3,089 candidates provisionally qualified for DM programmes and 1,628 for MCh programmes.

stories.title: MCC announces a special stray vacancy round for NEET UG
stories.summary: The Medical Counselling Committee will run a special stray vacancy round for MBBS, BDS and BSc Nursing seats left empty after regular NEET UG 2026 counselling. Registration opens on November 2 and the process runs until November 16.

stories.title: Nearly 2,000 MBBS seats remain empty after counselling
stories.summary: About 2,000 MBBS seats are still vacant after several rounds of NEET UG 2026 counselling, with Karnataka, Telangana, West Bengal and Rajasthan each reporting over 100. States and colleges are asking the NMC for more rounds, amid concerns over high fees.

stories.title: Maharashtra revises its NEET PG round 1 schedule
stories.summary: Maharashtra's State CET Cell has revised the NEET PG 2026 CAP round 1 schedule for MD and MS seats at government and private colleges. Choice filling begins on November 2, and the first selection list will be declared on November 5.

stories.title: Parliament's education committee reviews NEET UG exam integrity
stories.summary: After the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and exam cancellation, India's parliamentary education committee has begun a formal review of exam security and the functioning of the National Testing Agency. Recommendations are expected to change how the exam is run and monitored.

stories.title: An expert lays out how to prepare for CAT 2026
stories.summary: Careers360 sets out preparation advice for CAT 2026, a 120-minute exam with verbal ability and reading comprehension, data interpretation and logical reasoning, and quantitative ability sections. An expert recommends consistent mock tests, accuracy and time management.

stories.title: Will CBSE 2027 board exams clash with JEE Main
stories.summary: Students sitting both CBSE Class 10 or 12 boards and JEE Main 2027 want to know if the dates overlap. JEE Main session dates are out, but CBSE has not yet confirmed its final subject-wise date sheet, Physics Wallah notes.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu NEET PG counselling schedule is out
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu has released its NEET PG 2026 counselling schedule, with round 1 registration starting at tnmedicalselection.net, according to a Shiksha headline. The full article was blocked to us, so only the headline was available.

stories.title: UK raises student visa money requirements from November 30
stories.summary: From November 30, UK student visa applicants studying in London must show 1,570 pounds a month for living costs, up from 1,529, or up to 14,130 pounds for nine months. Those outside London need 1,203 pounds a month, under Statement of Changes HC 584.

stories.title: UK moves to a two-tier Graduate visa
stories.summary: The UK will keep the two-year Graduate visa only for students at selected universities, while others get 18 months from January 2027. The government has not named the qualifying universities. Nigeria accounted for 20,604 Graduate route approvals in the year to June 2026.

stories.title: New Zealand tightens student visa rules
stories.summary: Immigration New Zealand changed its student visa rules from October 27, ending unlimited work hours for research master's students and strengthening English language assessment. It also expanded its power to temporarily suspend application processing.

stories.title: Australia signals a review of student visa rules
stories.summary: Australia's government is preparing to revisit parts of its student visa policy as universities face a projected 2 billion dollar revenue shortfall. The concern is that tougher controls are discouraging genuine applicants to one of the country's biggest export industries.

stories.title: Canada reminds international students when they may work
stories.summary: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada says international students can work only if their study permit conditions allow it, with off-campus work capped at 24 hours a week during classes. Breaking the rules can cost students their status and lead to removal.

stories.title: Irish court overturns a Gazan student's visa refusal
stories.summary: Ireland's High Court overturned the refusal of a student visa to Shaymaa Abudalu, who had a fully funded place at University College Cork. The court heard the decision-maker failed to consider her English proficiency evidence and financial form, The PIE News reports.

stories.title: UK international student levy of 925 pounds to start in 2028
stories.summary: England plans a 925 pound annual levy per eligible international student from August 2028, expected to raise 445 million pounds in its first year. Nigeria's Petroleum Technology Development Fund has pointed to Germany and France as alternatives.

stories.title: Wisconsin's universities see an 11% drop in international students
stories.summary: An 11% fall in international students drove an overall enrolment dip across the Universities of Wisconsin system, which has 164,579 students, the Wisconsin State Journal reports. The rest of the article sits behind a paywall.

stories.title: Experts say MBBS abroad consultants exploit a vague regulator
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission gave ambiguous answers to aspiring doctors asking whether a six-year MBBS in Georgia would qualify them for India's foreign graduate exam. Legal experts allege this lets consultants mislead students, the Hindustan Times reports.

stories.title: DRDO chief tells IIT Delhi students to come back after studying abroad
stories.summary: Students going abroad should return and give back to the nation, DRDO's Binay Kumar Das told students at the inauguration of IIT Delhi's Open House. He urged them never to forget their roots and to carry Indian culture with them.

stories.title: Swapping China for India is not diversification, Australian op-ed argues
stories.summary: A Future Campus opinion piece argues Australian universities recruiting more Indian students to reduce dependence on China are only shifting their vulnerability. It notes China made up 23% of international students in the year to August 2026.

stories.title: Glasgow medical offer stalls on three UK visa refusals
stories.summary: A 25-year-old Afghan woman with a place and funding for medical education at the University of Glasgow has been refused a UK student visa three times, University Herald reports. Conflicting reasons for the refusals have left her unable to start.

stories.title: NMMSS scholarship deadline extended to November 15
stories.summary: The Ministry of Education has extended applications for the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme 2026-27 to November 15 on the National Scholarship Portal. Institute verification runs until November 30 and district-level verification must finish by December 15.

stories.title: AICTE opens Saraswati Scholarship applications for girls
stories.summary: AICTE's Saraswati Scholarship gives girl students in BBA, BCA and BMS courses at approved institutions Rs 25,000 a year for up to three years. Family income must not exceed Rs 8 lakh, and existing beneficiaries can apply for renewal.

stories.title: Tata Capital Pankh Scholarship opens for 2026-27
stories.summary: Tata Capital's Pankh Scholarship covers 80% to 100% of tuition fees, up to Rs 18,000, for students from economically weaker sections in Class 11, Class 12, undergraduate, diploma and ITI courses. The last date to apply is November 15.

stories.title: Pune university offers full fee waivers to students from the Northeast
stories.summary: Pimpri Chinchwad University in Pune is offering eight scholarships with a 100% tuition fee waiver, one for a meritorious student from each of the eight North Eastern states. Applicants must meet the university's eligibility criteria.

stories.title: Six scholarships for Indian students in 2026-27
stories.summary: The Hindustan Gazette lists six scholarship programmes from foundations, companies and philanthropies, citing Buddy4Study. They include full tuition support, medical education help and free coaching for exams such as CUET, JEE, CAT and CLAT, with varying deadlines.

stories.title: ETH Zurich opens its 2027 Excellence Scholarship
stories.summary: ETH Zurich has opened applications for its 2027 Excellence Scholarship and Opportunity Programme, a fully funded master's open to all countries. It covers tuition, pays a living stipend of CHF 12,000 per semester and includes mentoring.

stories.title: Khaama Press checks which scholarships Afghan students can still use
stories.summary: Khaama Press has verified scholarship routes for Afghan students against official websites. Options include University of the People's free online degree for women inside Afghanistan, Erasmus Mundus master's places and paid Marie Sklodowska-Curie doctoral posts.

stories.title: Two Cambodian students win ASEAN Scholarships to Singapore
stories.summary: Sa Sokritthi and Sok Moniketsya from Cambodia have won ASEAN Scholarships to study in Singapore after written tests and interviews. The four-year award covers secondary and pre-university education leading to the Singapore-Cambridge A-Level or equivalent.

stories.title: A guide to scholarships in China for international students
stories.summary: Academia Mag rounds up fully and partly funded scholarships in China that can cover tuition, accommodation, monthly stipends and medical insurance. They are open to international applicants at undergraduate, master's and doctoral level.

stories.title: Iowa opens applications for groups to hand out federal tax credit scholarships
stories.summary: Iowa nonprofits have until December 11 to apply to distribute K-12 scholarships under the new federal Education Freedom Tax Credit, Governor Kim Reynolds announced. The programme is set to begin in 2027.

stories.title: Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies offers funded places to Arab graduates
stories.summary: The Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies is offering up to five fully funded scholarships to graduate students from Arab countries, according to an Al-Fanar Media headline. The article was blocked to us, so only the headline was available.

stories.title: IIM Bangalore places every student in summer placements
stories.summary: All 608 participating students in IIM Bangalore's PGP and PGPBA 2026-28 batches received summer offers from 128 organisations. Consulting made up 308 offers, or 50.7%, with Accenture Strategy leading at 123.

stories.title: IIM Ahmedabad wraps up summer placements with 230 roles
stories.summary: IIM Ahmedabad's summer placement process for its 2026-28 PGP batch ran from October 23 to 30 in a hybrid format. Recruiters offered more than 230 roles across three clusters, from consulting and banking to healthcare and renewable energy.

stories.title: IIT Guwahati and Tata Electronics team up on semiconductor training
stories.summary: IIT Guwahati will offer diploma-level training and BTech-level programmes in semiconductor assembly, testing, marking and packaging with Tata Electronics. The courses include hands-on training aimed at roles in the chip industry.

stories.title: Fewer IIT and IIM graduates start companies in 2026
stories.summary: Only 79 IIT and 20 IIM alumni founded tech startups between January and August 2026, Tracxn data shows, against 307 and 71 in all of 2025. Tracxn cautions the figures are not like-for-like and the 2026 count may rise.

stories.title: University of Oregon plans to save $65 million a year
stories.summary: The University of Oregon's proposal would cut 18 academic programmes and more than 100 jobs, among other changes, to save $65 million a year, Higher Ed Dive reports. Only the teaser was available to us.

stories.title: Lincoln makes lecture recording compulsory and the union objects
stories.summary: The University of Lincoln now requires lecturers to record sessions, citing accessibility. The UCU has declared a dispute and launched a boycott, worried recordings could be used in misconduct cases or to replace striking staff, Times Higher Education reports.

stories.title: UT Southern climbs 11 places in US News rankings
stories.summary: The University of Tennessee Southern rose to No. 43 in the 2027 US News Regional Colleges South category, from No. 54, and from 19th to 12th among top public schools there. Chancellor Melinda Arnold called it the story of an institution on the rise.

stories.title: Rutgers-Camden makes WalletHub's New Jersey top ten
stories.summary: Rutgers University-Camden ranks in the top ten New Jersey colleges in a WalletHub study comparing 738 institutions on selectivity, cost and financing, faculty resources and other factors. The study was published on October 12.

stories.title: Moldova's universities enrol 2,433 international students
stories.summary: Students from 31 countries enrolled at Moldovan universities this year, mainly from Romania, Ukraine, India and Israel. The most popular programmes are psychology, law, medicine, early years education and dentistry, Logos Press reports.

stories.title: University of Gdansk wins NAWA funding to support international students
stories.summary: The University of Gdansk's International Academic and Career Integration Centre project has received funding from Poland's National Agency for Academic Exchange under Welcome to Poland 2026. It will train staff and support international students.

stories.title: REVA University holds its first literature festival
stories.summary: REVA University opened The First Chapter, a two-day literature festival, on October 30 with author interactions, panels, poetry, book talks and Kannada theatre. The university also honoured students for academic excellence.

stories.title: AICTE launches four schemes for technical institutions
stories.summary: AICTE has launched IDEA Lab, MODROBS, Margdarshan and a conference grant scheme for 2026-27, covering labs, infrastructure modernisation, mentoring and conference funding. Chairman Yogesh Singh said they aim to reach institutions across districts, not only established centres.

stories.title: UGC flags 78 Karnataka colleges over unpaid fee refunds
stories.summary: The UGC has flagged 78 Karnataka colleges and universities over 132 unresolved fee refund complaints from 2020 to 2025, involving students who cancelled admission in time. It has asked the Governor's office to ensure compliance.

stories.title: Supreme Court to decide if PhD years count as teaching experience
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has reserved judgment on whether PhD years count toward the eight years of experience needed for Associate Professor posts. The case concerns Priya Varghese's appointment at Kannur University, upheld by the Kerala High Court in 2023.

stories.title: NMC withdraws its medical education standards rules
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission has withdrawn MSMER-2023, which allowed fines of up to Rs 5 lakh on individual faculty for false information. The rating board can still penalise institutions up to Rs 1 crore, but The Hindu asks whether that will deter individuals.

stories.title: BPSC cancels 1,711 medical college assistant professor posts
stories.summary: The Bihar Public Service Commission has cancelled advertisements for 1,711 Assistant Professor posts in medical colleges after the health department withdrew its requests. Fresh advertisements are being prepared, but no date has been given.

stories.title: Karnataka drafts rules to curb coaching centres
stories.summary: Karnataka's draft coaching centre rules would bar children under 15, cap coaching at five hours a day and make refunds mandatory for students who leave a course midway. The rules target academic pressure, arbitrary fees and misleading ads.

stories.title: Jamia students end an 18-day protest
stories.summary: Students at Jamia Millia Islamia ended an 18-day protest and hunger strike after the administration agreed to reinstate the Students' Union, with elections in 2027. It also agreed to withdraw protest-related disciplinary actions and bans.

stories.title: UGC asks campuses to mark BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week
stories.summary: The UGC has asked colleges and universities to observe BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week from November 1 to 7. Activities under Mission LiFE will cover seven themes, including energy conservation, water management and waste reduction.

stories.title: Himachal gets 320 more postgraduate medical seats
stories.summary: Himachal Pradesh will add 320 postgraduate medical seats, backed by Rs 415 crore from the Centre, Governor Kavinder Gupta said. He said the seats will strengthen medical education and improve the supply of specialist doctors in the state.

stories.title: Should universities teach or research
stories.summary: A Hindu opinion piece asks whether institutions can do justice to both teaching and research, and whether great teachers become great researchers. It notes NEP 2020 describes research-intensive universities, teaching-intensive universities and autonomous colleges.

stories.title: US finalises its college accreditation overhaul
stories.summary: The US Education Department has finalised rules overhauling college accreditation, including new standards on intellectual diversity and how accreditors police civil rights law. Critics argue the changes politicise decisions on which colleges receive federal aid, Inside Higher Ed reports.

stories.title: Former for-profit college students sue over undischarged loans
stories.summary: Former students of for-profit colleges, including those owned by Career Education Corporation and Education Management Corporation, filed a class action against the US Education Department for refusing to discharge their loans. Student Defense represents them.

stories.title: What if community colleges had real endowments
stories.summary: An Inside Higher Ed columnist takes up a question from Northern Essex Community College president Lane Glenn about community colleges capturing a small share of rich universities' endowment gains. He argues tax exemptions are a public subsidy that should bring public obligations.

stories.title: Colleges keep adding football programmes
stories.summary: Whittier College in California brought football back this fall after cutting it in 2022, with 96 players on the roster at a college of under 1,000 students. Officials count the enrolment boost as an off-the-field win, Inside Higher Ed reports.
